newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foot and mouth disease hits Taiwan's pork industry.
newsitem.headline: Foot and mouth disease hits Taiwan's pork industry.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday banned all pork exports following an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease in the island's hog population, spelling huge losses for exporters.

Taiwan's Council of Agriculture announced earlier on Thursday that laboratory results confirmed an outbreak of foot and mouth on the island and warned it faced a daunting task in trying to eliminate the disease.
"Laboratory tests have determined that a disease found in the hog population is indeed foot and mouth disease," an official of the cabinet agency told Reuters.
A statement issued by the Council said all exports of fresh and frozen pork would be banned temporarily -- effectively cutting off the island's pork export industry.
The council estimated that Taiwan exported six million out of the 14 million hogs it bred each year.
According to an industry survey, the hog industry's net value stood at T$89 billion ($3.24 billion) in 1994, representing 20 percent of Taiwan's farm market and 60 percent of the livestock sector.
The Council said instances of the disease had been found in nine Taiwan counties and more than 20 breeding farms.
"This is an airborne virus that has a very high tolerance to sanitation measures," a council official said.
Furthermore, Taiwan only has about 40,000 foot and mouth vaccines available, which can hardly curb the disease's outbreak, experts said.
"There are simply not enough vaccines to go around," another council official said.
The Council said it would import more vaccines immediately.
Japan, Taiwan's largest pork export market, has not been infected by the disease and was expected to impose its own ban on pork shipments from Taiwan, experts said.

Japan had been importing some 16,000 tonnes of fresh and frozen pork from Taiwan per month despite Tokyo's imposition of a special "emergency" import tariff to limit imports and protect local breeders.
Taiwan's pork exports to Japan represented about 69 percent of the island's total pork exports. South Korea was another major destination.
Japan imported about 183,494 tonnes of pork from Taiwan in 1995, ranking Taiwan its largest supplier.
Other suppliers -- mainly the United States, Canada and European countries -- are likely to take over Taiwan's market shares, Japanese industry sources said.

Taiwan's pork exports had been limited mainly to Japan because both were battling hog cholera, another highly contagious disease that has seen scattered outbreaks in Taiwan's huge stockyards for years.
Japan has launched a campaign to eliminate hog cholera by 1999, forcing Taiwan to consider a similar programme for fear of losing its main export market.
Japan has said it would ban pork imports from cholera-infected areas once it gained control over the disease.
Analysts said the export ban also would hurt many of Taiwan's pork-related downstream businesses, particularly the feed industry.
They said the ban may prompt corn buyers to cut the island's imports of feed corn by about one-fifth.
